name: Irving Berlin
tagline: Immigrant street singer who wrote 'God Bless America' and 'White Christmas'

born.place: Russian Empire (family lived in Tolochin, present-day Belarus)

immigration.detail: Fleeing anti-Jewish persecution, the Beilin family emigrated in 1893, passing through Ellis Island and settling on Manhattan's Lower East Side. After his father died, young Israel left home and sang for pennies in Bowery saloons.

hero_image.credit: Al Aumuller, New York World-Telegram & Sun, 1948 (Library of Congress)

summary: A five-year-old refugee who could never read music, Irving Berlin wrote an estimated 1,500 songs across six decades, including the unofficial national anthem 'God Bless America' and the best-selling single of all time, 'White Christmas'.

biography.text: Irving Berlin was born Israel Beilin on May 11, 1888, in the Russian Empire; his family was living in Tolochin, in present-day Belarus, when they fled anti-Jewish violence and emigrated to New York in 1893. His father, a cantor, died when he was thirteen, and the boy left home to earn money as a singing waiter and street singer on the Bowery, where he taught himself to pick out tunes on the piano using only the black keys.

His first published song, 'Marie from Sunny Italy' (1907), earned him 37 cents and a printer's error that renamed him 'I. Berlin'. In 1911 'Alexander's Ragtime Band' became an international sensation and made him, at 23, the most famous songwriter in America. He co-founded the American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) in 1914 and built the Music Box Theatre on Broadway in 1921 to stage his own revues.

Drafted into the U.S. Army in 1918, Berlin wrote the soldier show Yip Yip Yaphank at Camp Upton and composed 'God Bless America', which he set aside for twenty years before Kate Smith introduced it on Armistice Day 1938. He assigned all royalties from the song to the Boy Scouts and Girl Scouts of America. During the Second World War he toured the world with the all-soldier revue This Is the Army, which raised millions for Army Emergency Relief and earned him the Medal for Merit.

'White Christmas', written for the 1942 film Holiday Inn, won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and became the best-selling single ever recorded. His Broadway scores included Annie Get Your Gun (1946), with 'There's No Business Like Show Business', and Call Me Madam (1950). Jerome Kern's famous verdict was that 'Irving Berlin has no place in American music—he is American music.'

Berlin received a Congressional Gold Medal in 1955 for 'God Bless America' and other patriotic songs, and the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Gerald Ford in 1977. He lived quietly in New York in his final decades and died at his home on September 22, 1989, at the age of 101.

achievements.title: 'Alexander's Ragtime Band'
achievements.description: The song that launched the ragtime craze worldwide and made Berlin famous at 23.

achievements.title: Co-founded ASCAP
achievements.description: A founding member of the American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, which secured royalties for songwriters.

achievements.title: 'God Bless America'
achievements.description: Written during his Army service in 1918 and introduced by Kate Smith in 1938; royalties were assigned to the Boy Scouts and Girl Scouts of America.

achievements.title: 'White Christmas'
achievements.description: Academy Award winner for Best Original Song and, in Bing Crosby's recording, the best-selling single of all time.

achievements.title: Annie Get Your Gun
achievements.description: Broadway score featuring 'There's No Business Like Show Business' and 'Anything You Can Do'.

achievements.title: Catalogue of roughly 1,500 songs
achievements.description: Including scores for 19 Broadway shows and 18 Hollywood films, all composed without the ability to read or write musical notation.

timeline.description: Kate Smith sings it on her radio show on the eve of Armistice Day; it becomes a second national anthem.

timeline.title: Dies in New York at 101
timeline.description: Dies at his Beekman Place home; Broadway theatres dim their lights in tribute.

quotes.text: Irving Berlin has no place in American music—he is American music.
quotes.context: Composer Jerome Kern, in a frequently quoted assessment reproduced in Berlin's Songwriters Hall of Fame profile

fun_facts.text: Berlin could play the piano only in the key of F-sharp, so he used a specially built 'transposing piano' with a lever that shifted the keyboard to other keys.
All royalties from 'God Bless America' go to the Boy Scouts and Girl Scouts through a fund he created in 1940.

discussion_prompts: Berlin arrived speaking no English and never learned to read music. What does his story suggest about talent, opportunity and hard work?
Why do you think an immigrant wrote the songs many Americans consider the most 'American' of all?
Listen to the 1911 recording of 'Alexander's Ragtime Band'. What sounds modern, and what sounds like another era?

media.title: 'Alexander's Ragtime Band' – Arthur Collins & Byron Harlan, Victor Records (1911)
media.description: One of the first hit recordings of Berlin's breakthrough song, made within weeks of its publication.
media.annotation: Recorded acoustically into a horn before microphones existed. The crackle is the sound of 1911.

media.title: 'That Revolutionary Rag' (1919)
media.description: A topical rag Berlin wrote in the year after his Army service.
media.annotation: Berlin wrote hundreds of songs about the news of the day; most are forgotten, which makes the survivors more remarkable.
media.rights_note: Pre-1923 recordings entered the U.S. public domain in 2022 under the Music Modernization Act; confirm the exact recording date on the file page before republishing.

review_notes.finding: We could not find Irving Berlin on the Kennedy Center Honors recipient lists for 1978 or any other year. Recommend verifying with the Kennedy Center before publishing.
Most published biographies date his naturalization to 1918, the year he was drafted. Recommend checking naturalization records.
